title: Batch 12 Spinal Failure Mode Concepts
patient_facing_caution: These are educational pattern-recognition concepts, not diagnostic claims.

concepts.summary: Disc is often not the primary pain generator. Deep ligaments (PLL, ALL, flavum, facet capsules) are poorly vascularised and slow to regenerate — they generate deep, postural, diffuse pain. This is structural + microcirculatory + fascia failure. The 4-axis failure model explicitly separates disc from ligament from nerve from stasis.

Hypotonic spinal ligament = spinal prolapse. Same Qi-deficiency root as uterine prolapse, pelvic floor insufficiency, varicosities. Common in women, postpartum, chronic fatigue. Needs holding tone before movement — same sequencing as prolapse management.

Facet joint pain is capsulo-ligamentous pain, not classic joint/OA pain. Pain borne by capsule + deep paraspinal fascia + ligamentous tension system, not articular surface. Apply Yin/Yang ligament sub-typing. Support agents work systemically via circulation — not facet-specific targeting needed.

Disc, ligament, and fascia are functional categories, not exclusive anatomical targets. Support acts systemically via circulation and matrix integration. Engine should score functional failure modes, not assign interventions based on anatomy alone.

key_principles: Pain emerges from functional failure modes, not anatomy alone.
The disc is often a passive witness.
The structure may fail because it cannot hold — not because it is inflamed.
